Using the energy-time uncertainty principle:

ΔE · Δt ≈ ħ

**Calculate the energy width (uncertainty) of each state:**

ħ ≈ 6.58 × 10⁻¹⁶ eV·s

**State 1** (τ₁ = 10⁻⁹ s):
ΔE₁ ≈ ħ/τ₁ = (6.58 × 10⁻¹⁶)/(10⁻⁹) ≈ 6.58 × 10⁻⁷ eV

**State 2** (τ₂ = 10⁻⁸ s):
ΔE₂ ≈ ħ/τ₂ = (6.58 × 10⁻¹⁶)/(10⁻⁸) ≈ 6.58 × 10⁻⁸ eV

**Condition to resolve the two levels:**

To clearly distinguish two energy levels, their energy separation must be **larger than the energy widths** of the states (otherwise the levels overlap due to their natural linewidth).

The energy difference must satisfy:
$$E_2 - E_1 > \Delta E_1 \approx 6.6 \times 10^{-7} \text{ eV}$$

(The larger of the two widths, ~10⁻⁷ eV, dominates.)

**Check the options:**

- (A) 10⁻⁸ eV → too small (< 10⁻⁷)
- (B) 10⁻⁴ eV → **larger than 10⁻⁷ eV** ✓
- (C) 10⁻¹¹ eV → far too small
- (D) 10⁻⁹ eV → too small

Only **10⁻⁴ eV** is greater than the natural linewidth, so the two levels can be clearly resolved.

Answer: B
